rows.claim: NO roster-epoch concept ships in my sources. Grepping Olamnit.Shared/Kv/Election/ and Olamnit.Shared/Kv/Capabilities/ case-insensitively for the vocabulary {roster, epoch, exclu*, revok*, revocation, ban, genesis, nonce, reintegrat*, founder, manifest, run_id, blocklist, denylist, expel, evict, rejoin, quarantin, era} returns ZERO hits in Kv/Capabilities/ and, in Kv/Election/, only the word 'operator' inside a comment. ABSENCE SCOPED VERBATIM to those two directories at pin 02bcc20 with that exact vocabulary; I could not read the rest of the repo, so this is not a repo-scope absence.

The election's versioning primitive is a per-domain monotone int64 TERM, not a roster epoch: DecisionRecord carries exactly (DomainId, Term, DecisionId, Winner, Protocol) and NO membership set, membership hash, roster version, or nonce. Nothing in a shipped decision record binds the decision to the membership that produced it.

The durable decision table columns are exactly (domain_id, term, decision_id, winner, protocol, decided_utc) as written by the shipped INSERT — no membership, no roster epoch, no nonce, no signature. A roster epoch therefore cannot be persisted in the shipped decision log without a schema change.

Membership is FIXED AT CONSTRUCTION and immutable for the life of the election object: both RaftElection and PbftElection take IReadOnlyList<string> membership as a primary-constructor parameter, and the IElectionDomain seam exposes only {Id, Protocol, DecideAsync, ConfirmTermAsync} — there is NO add-member, remove-member, or change-membership API. Changing membership means constructing a new election instance; nothing in these sources records that a change occurred, versions it, or binds prior decisions to the old set.

Membership entries are OPAQUE STRINGS ('a','b','c') and are never compared against, or mapped to, any Ed25519 public key. In PbftElection the trust anchor is consulted only as trustAnchor.TrustedKeys.Count == 0 — the membership ids and the trusted key set are two unrelated collections. A shipped election therefore cannot bind a member id to a key, and so cannot express 'this node, identified by its key, is/is not in the roster'.

CODE/COMMENT DISAGREEMENT (M-32). The doc comment on PbftElection.GatheredPrepares asserts 'each prepare's signer must be a trusted peer key — verified via trustAnchor'. The CODE never verifies any prepare, any signer, or any signature: GatheredPrepares is a plain public settable int, and the only trust-anchor use in the whole class is the emptiness test `trustAnchor.TrustedKeys.Count == 0`. The Byzantine authentication the comment claims is NOT implemented in this file; the quorum count is injected by the host/test.

Raft's liveness input is likewise an unauthenticated injected number: `public int ReachableVoters { get; set; }` with no bound and no provenance. Counterexample constructed against 'quorum protects the decision' (M-36): `new RaftElection(d, ["a","b","c"], log) { ReachableVoters = 99 }` passes `votes*2 > membership.Count` and decides. Nothing in RaftElection.cs constrains ReachableVoters to <= membership.Count.

Raft's liveness check is DEFAULT-OPEN, not fail-closed: `int voters = ReachableVoters > 0 ? ReachableVoters : membership.Count;` — an unset ReachableVoters (0) is silently read as 'ALL members reachable', so a freshly-constructed RaftElection always reaches quorum. Zero reachable voters is indistinguishable from full reachability at this line.

THE THRESHOLD ARITHMETIC: Raft quorum is a strict majority of the FIXED constructed membership — `votes * 2 > membership.Count` (denominator = membership.Count, i.e. the epoch's fixed N, never 'who is live now'); the numerator is the injected reachable count. Below quorum ⇒ LivenessTimeout, never a Byzantine refusal.

THE THRESHOLD ARITHMETIC: PBFT computes f = (membership.Count - 1) / 3 and Quorum = 2f + 1, both over the FIXED constructed membership count — the denominator IS the epoch's fixed N, not a live-set count. membership.Count < 4 refuses with QuorumUnattainable ('membership {n} < 3f+1 minimum (4)'). This is the one shipped arithmetic that matches a 'threshold over fixed membership N' requirement.

Below-quorum PBFT returns ElectionOutcomeKind.QuorumUnattainable as a value and NEVER falls back to the crash-fault path — verified by code (the guard returns before any log.DecideAsync call) and by test. This 'refusal, never a downgrade' property IS shipped and is testable.

A SINGLE ELECTED DECISION per (domain, decision_id) IS shipped and IS bindable: the compare-and-set is across ALL terms (the prior lookup scans every term for the decision_id, deterministic lowest-term-first), so a later term never contradicts a committed decision; the loser receives the durable winner + the durable term. This is the strongest primitive in my slice for 'one elected decision other subsystems bind to'.

The decision key is (domain_id, decision_id) — a caller-supplied opaque string pair. Nothing in the shipped code parses, validates, or interprets DecisionId or Proposal. A roster epoch COULD therefore be smuggled into a decision_id string, but no shipped code would enforce, order, or bind it — the log would treat 'roster/epoch-7' as an arbitrary label.

There IS a shipped binding surface from a subsystem to an elected decision: KV PublishOnceAsync(key, payload, domain) routes through the registered election domain and refuses with KvOutcome.ElectionRequired when no domain is registered; ordinary commutative Puts are unaffected. This is exercised end-to-end in the battery.

THE TRUST ANCHOR IS GROW-ONLY: IPeerSetTrustAnchor exposes exactly four members — TrustedKeys (get), TryPublishRootKey, TryAddPeerKey, IsTrusted. There is NO remove, revoke, replace, clear, expire, or version operation on the interface OR on the PeerSetTrustAnchor class. Grep of Kv/Capabilities/ for {TryRemove, Revoke, Unpublish, Delete, Clear, Reset} returns zero hits. Once a key is added it is trusted for the object's lifetime. PERMANENT EXCLUSION OF A NODE IS NOT EXPRESSIBLE at the shipped trust anchor.

The trust anchor is IN-MEMORY ONLY — a `List<byte[]> _keys` behind a lock, with no store seam, no constructor-injected persistence, and no load/save path anywhere in the class. Unlike the election decision log (which has IElectionDecisionStore + a PGlite backend), there is no IPeerSetTrustAnchorStore in Kv/Capabilities/. The 'publish-once root that can never be replaced' therefore holds only within one process lifetime; a restart yields an empty, fail-closed anchor that must be re-populated by whatever code calls TryPublishRootKey.

'HIGHER AUTHORITY' IS NOT EXPRESSIBLE at the trust anchor. TryAddPeerKey(ReadOnlySpan<byte> publicKey) takes ONLY a public key — no signature, no grant, no proof that the root (or anyone) authorized the addition. The only gate is `if (!_rootPublished) return false`. Any caller holding the anchor reference can add any key. The root's 'publish-once' privilege is solely that slot 0 cannot be overwritten; it confers no veto or signing authority over subsequent additions.

The 'root first' ordering of TrustedKeys is DECORATIVE for authorization: IsTrusted ORs a FixedTimeEquals over every slot with no positional weighting, and the only other shipped consumer (PbftElection) reads only .Count. No shipped code in my sources treats slot 0 differently from slot k during verification. The doc comment calls the first slot 'the publish-once ROOT key (element 9's degenerate single-decree)' — that is a DOC assertion about intent; the code gives the root no superior verification standing.

Every anchored key is a FULL SELF-MINTING AUTHORITY: KvCaveats.MintGrant(IDeviceSealKey key, resource, audience, identity, exp, verbs, tbl, kpfx) seals a grant with the holder's OWN key and arbitrary caveat values, and PeerSetAmuletVerifier accepts any grant whose embedded key IsTrusted. There is no attenuation-from-root, no delegation chain, and no check that a peer's self-chosen resource/audience/scope was ever granted to it. Combined with the absence of removal, a compromised anchored key can mint unlimited fresh grants indefinitely within the process lifetime — expiry cannot contain it because the holder simply re-mints.

SAFE REINTEGRATION of a returning node has no shipped surface in my sources: TryAddPeerKey is idempotent and unconditional (re-adding an already-present key returns true with no state change, no epoch bump, no history), and the election objects have no rejoin/catch-up/fence path. Reintegration is indistinguishable from initial admission — there is nothing to make it 'safe' at this layer.

GENESIS CANNOT BE EXPRESSED with the shipped seal shape: the verifier reads exactly ONE PubKeyHex and ONE SignatureHex from a Seal and verifies a single Ed25519 signature over the canonical-CBOR payload. A genesis manifest 'signed by all N founders' requires N signatures over one document; the shipped Seal/verifier surface is single-signer, with no multi-signature aggregation, threshold-signature, or signature-list shape anywhere in Kv/Capabilities/.

No genesis_hash, run_id, or run nonce exists in the shipped decision surface: DecisionRecord has no nonce field, Term is an in-process int64 counter raised only by AdvanceTerm() and Math.Max(_term, log.HighestTerm(domain)), and there is no freshness value derived from or bound to any founding document. A non-circular genesis_hash->run_id binding has NO shipped carrier in my sources.

The election decision log is HARD-CEILINGED at 100,000 decisions per domain (constructor default maxDecisionsPerDomain), returning KvOutcome.StorageCeilingReached at the ceiling. No archive/prune/compact API exists in Kv/Election/ — the comment says 'archive is an explicit operator act (FR-008)' but ships no operator surface. A very-high-cycle-count design that consumes one decision per epoch/batch hits an absorbing refusal state at 100k epochs per domain with no shipped exit.

The ceiling is enforced against ONE INSTANCE'S LOADED VIEW, and the code's own comment bands the residual: 'N live logs over one store can jointly overshoot by at most N-1 decisions before their next reload'. Additionally the in-memory cache retains every loaded decision for the process lifetime (Dictionary keyed (Term, DecisionId) per domain), so a long-running node's election RAM grows monotonically toward the ceiling.

COULD NOT VERIFY (load-bearing): the single-winner-across-terms guarantee of the PGlite store rests on a claimed unique index. The comment states 'The DURABLE arbiter is the kv_election_decision_single_winner_idx unique index on (domain_id, decision_id) ... contradictory durable rows are impossible-by-construction'. The CODE issues a bare `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` naming NO constraint, and the index is defined in KvSubstrateSchema.Ddl (Kv/Store/), which is OUTSIDE my slice. rows.claim: TWO DISTINCT capability dialects ship side by side in my sources, not one. (1) The amulet dialect: string 'k=v' caveats over an HMAC chain inside an Ed25519 seal (Olamnit.Shared/Yngenios/Seal/). (2) macaroon-v2: a binary tag-numbered caveat wire + HMAC tail chain, pinned in conformance/macaroon-v2/. The macaroon-v2 README states macaroon-v2 'is the ONE converged capability dialect - it supersedes the amulet HMAC-chain + Ed25519-seal dialect for **mesh capability tokens** (the amulet code stays for its existing fetch-from-store surface)'. NOTE: I am quoting a README (doc), not code; the C# MacaroonV2Verifier named there lives at Olamnit.Shared.Tests/Kv/... + Olamnit.Shared/Kv/, OUTSIDE my slice, so I could not verify the code behind that claim. A mesh-segment capability bound would therefore land on macaroon-v2, NOT on the amulet caveat set.

AMULET DIALECT - the closed caveat key set is exactly six, enforced by a C# switch whose default arm refuses: exp, scope, audience, resource, tbl, kpfx. Any other key returns (false, "unknown caveat key: {k}"). This is CODE, not a comment.

AMULET DIALECT - the caveat set HAS been extended once before, and the mechanism is recorded in code as an APPEND after the existing keys: a source comment at Macaroon.cs:71-75 states 'Feature #057 (T014, R-6): the KV caveat extension - tbl (per-table) + kpfx (key-prefix range). Appended AFTER the existing four in the fixed mint order (exp -> scope -> audience -> resource -> tbl -> kpfx) so every already-minted macaroon verifies unchanged, and OLD verifiers refuse the new keys (below) and thus fail closed - the rollout only ever tightens.' I am quoting a COMMENT. The compatibility argument it makes is structurally sound against the code I can see: a macaroon minted without tbl/kpfx still hits only the four original switch arms, and an old verifier's default arm refuses an unknown key rather than ignoring it. So the precedent for a 7th appended key exists and is documented.

CONTRADICTION (code vs code): the shipped minter's caveat order is scope -> exp -> audience -> resource, NOT the 'fixed mint order exp -> scope -> audience -> resource' asserted by the Macaroon.cs:73 comment and pinned by the conformance vector. AmuletMinter.Mint builds the array literally as {$"scope={scope}", $"exp={exp:yyyy-MM-dd}", $"audience={audience}", $"resource={resourceId}"} under a comment reading 'Caveat order is signed - keep it stable.' The pinned vector grant-kv-caveats.json instead pins exp first. Since order is signed into both the HMAC chain and the CBOR array, the bytes AmuletMinter actually emits can never equal the pinned vector's canonical_hex. There is no single 'exact mint order' in this repo - the minter and the pinned corpus disagree.

AmuletMinter.Mint - the ONLY minter in my sources - has a fixed 6-parameter signature (IDeviceSealKey, string resourceId, string scope, string audience, DateOnly exp, string identity) and can mint ONLY the four original caveats. It has NO parameter and NO code path for tbl or kpfx, let alone a new key. Adding any 7th caveat key to a minted amulet requires either changing this signature or calling Macaroon.Create directly and hand-rolling the seal.

COUNTEREXAMPLE CONSTRUCTED (M-36) - the tbl and kpfx caveats are UNSATISFIABLE through the shipped Ed25519AmuletVerifier. Verify builds its enforcement context with exactly three entries: scope, audience, resource. It never populates 'tbl' or 'key'. So a macaroon carrying tbl=books hits Macaroon.cs:77, GetValueOrDefault("tbl") returns null != "books", refuse; a macaroon carrying kpfx=settings/ hits Macaroon.cs:82, context["key"] is absent so the 'is not string accessedKey' guard trips, refuse. The 057 caveat extension is enforceable only via some other caller that calls Macaroon.EnforceCaveats directly with a richer context - I could not see such a caller (it would be outside Seal/).

AMULET DIALECT - expiry granularity is a WHOLE DAY and nothing finer. The caveat value is parsed with DateOnly.TryParse, the enforcement parameter is DateOnly now, the comparison is 'if (now > exp)' (i.e. still valid THROUGHOUT the expiry day; expiry is inclusive), and the minter formats it '{exp:yyyy-MM-dd}'. A time-limited fallback measured in minutes or hours CANNOT be expressed by this caveat as it ships.

AMULET DIALECT - the exact enforcement API shapes are: IAmuletVerifier.Verify(Seal amulet, DateOnly now, string expectedScope, string expectedAudience) -> (bool Ok, string Reason); and Macaroon.EnforceCaveats(DateOnly now, IReadOnlyDictionary<string,string> context) -> (bool Ok, string Reason). Both are DateOnly-typed. Widening expiry to sub-day granularity is a BREAKING change to both public signatures, not an additive one.

The 'now' used for amulet expiry enforcement is supplied ENTIRELY by the caller - it is a DateOnly parameter threaded from IAmuletVerifier.Verify into Macaroon.EnforceCaveats. Within my sources (all six files under Yngenios/Seal/, read in full; search vocabulary: DateTime, TimeProvider, UtcNow, Today, IClock, Stopwatch, now, case-insensitive) there is no clock, no time provider, and no default. OPEN QUESTION: who supplies 'now' at each call site, and whether that source is monotonic, device-local, attacker-influenceable, or offline-skewable, is outside my slice and I could not verify it. This matters: a caller that passes a device-local date can be rolled back to un-expire an amulet.

COUNTEREXAMPLE CONSTRUCTED (M-36) - an OMITTED amulet caveat constrains NOTHING. EnforceCaveats is a foreach over the PRESENT caveats only; an empty caveat list falls straight through to return (true, "ok"). Nothing in Verify requires a scope, audience, exp, or resource caveat to be present. So a Seal minted with caveats=[] verifies OK against ANY expectedScope and ANY expectedAudience and NEVER expires. The security of this surface rests wholly on the minter always adding all four - there is no verifier-side floor.

The FetchDescriptor's Scope, Audience and IssuedForIdentity fields are SIGNED (they are in the CBOR signing payload) but NEVER ENFORCED. Ed25519AmuletVerifier cross-checks only ResourceId three ways (seal vs macaroon.Identifier vs descriptor.ResourceId). expectedScope/expectedAudience are compared against the CAVEATS, never against the descriptor. So a seal whose descriptor says Scope="admin" while its scope caveat says scope="kv" verifies OK under expectedScope="kv". The doc comment at Seal.cs:12-17 says the signature 'covers intent' - the code does not act on that intent.

AMULET DIALECT - a scope caveat DOES already exist in the closed set and IS enforced by exact ordinal equality against a verifier-supplied context value: 'if (context.GetValueOrDefault("scope") != v) return (false, ...)'. The verifier passes expectedScope straight into context["scope"] (AmuletVerifier.cs:114). So a mesh-segment bound CAN in principle ride the existing 'scope' key as an opaque string, provided every verifier call site supplies the matching segment value as expectedScope. The value is an uninterpreted string - no structure, no prefix semantics, no set membership.

Overloading the existing 'scope' caveat for a mesh-segment bound is CONSTRAINED, not free: scope is a SINGLE exact-match string already carrying an authorization scope value (e.g. "kv:read+write" in the pinned vector), and AmuletMinter emits exactly one scope caveat from one parameter. A segment bound would either have to be packed into that one string (changing its grammar and every expectedScope caller) or ride a new appended key. It cannot be added as a second independent scope caveat without both matching the same context["scope"] value.

The amulet corpus's UNKNOWN-KEY EXAMPLE is 'quota=100' - vector grant-refuse-unknown-caveat.json appends quota=100 as a 7th caveat after exp/scope/audience/resource/tbl/kpfx and pins expect "refuse:PermissionDenied". Therefore a newly-appended caveat key would collide with a pinned vector ONLY if it were named 'quota'. Any other name (e.g. 'seg', 'segment', 'path') does not collide with this vector - but ADDING it to the known set would still require regenerating this vector's neighbours only if the new key appears in them, which it would not.

An INDEPENDENT re-implementation of the amulet caveat enforcement EXISTS and must move in lockstep: tools/kv-conformance/verify_vectors.py carries its own hardcoded KNOWN_CAVEATS = {"exp", "scope", "audience", "resource", "tbl", "kpfx"} and its own enforce_caveats(). Its module docstring states it is 'deliberately NOT a port of the C# code: cross-runtime independence is the point (SC-004)'. Any 7th caveat key must be added HERE too or the Python CI step fails closed with 'unknown caveat key'.

DIVERGENCE between the two enforcement implementations of 'exp': C# uses DateOnly.TryParse(v, out exp) - which is CULTURE-SENSITIVE and accepts non-ISO forms (e.g. '12/31/2026' under en-US) - while the Python verifier uses date.fromisoformat(v), which accepts ISO-8601 only and RAISES (uncaught ValueError, not a fail-closed return) on anything else. The two do not agree on the set of well-formed exp values. The pinned vector only ever uses 'exp=2026-12-31', so no vector exercises this divergence.

The Python verifier's 'now' for expiry is a HARDCODED LITERAL date(2026, 7, 12) passed into enforce_caveats - it is not read from the vector's context and not the system clock. So the corpus's expiry semantics are pinned against a frozen date baked into the verifier source, not into the corpus. Any vector whose exp crosses that literal changes meaning only if the literal is edited.

COVERAGE GAP: the Python verifier runs caveat enforcement ONLY for grant-cbor vectors whose expect starts with 'refuse:'. For expect=="ok" grant vectors it checks canonical bytes + digest and returns (True, "ok") WITHOUT ever calling enforce_caveats. Consequently grant-kv-caveats.json - the one vector pinning the full six-caveat order - has its context field set to null and its SATISFIED-path enforcement is never exercised by this verifier. The corpus pins the BYTES of the full vocab, not its accept behaviour.

What the kv-substrate corpus PINS and how it is versioned: corpus-manifest.json carries corpus_version 1, vector_count 35, and a sha256 over each vector file's exact on-disk BYTES. The vectors themselves pin, per surface, canonical_hex + digest_hex + an expect of "ok" or "refuse:<closed outcome>". Two independent gates exist: verify_vectors.py (semantic re-encode) and verify_manifest.py (byte parity). The README states the corpus is 'FROZEN at first replication (US3, T042)' and that a change 'must regenerate them HERE first, bump corpus_version, and land the same-saga consumer updates together'.

COST of touching the amulet caveat surface, concretely (from the code, not the doc): a new caveat key forces (1) the C# switch arm in Macaroon.cs; (2) the verifier's context dictionary in AmuletVerifier.cs (else it is unsatisfiable, see the tbl/kpfx counterexample); (3) AmuletMinter's signature; (4) KNOWN_CAVEATS + enforce_caveats in the Python verifier; (5) regeneration of grant-kv-caveats.json AND grant-refuse-unknown-caveat.json (both embed the caveat list, its HMAC sig, canonical_hex and digest_hex); (6) their two sha256 pins in corpus-manifest.json; (7) a corpus_version bump per the stated change discipline; (8) the named-but-unseen consumer suites (Olamnit.Shared.Tests/Kv/GoldenVectorTests.cs, qhstate's frozen-import copy, buildkit's pytest verifier). Items 1-6 I verified in code/data; item 8 I am quoting the README consumer table.

MACAROON-V2 DIALECT - the closed caveat vocabulary is exactly SIX kinds, wire-tag-numbered 0..5, decoded from wire-roundtrip-full-vocab.json's token_hex: 0=time_before (bare 8-byte BE unix seconds, NO length prefix), 1=resource (len32+utf8 content_hash), 2=key (len32+utf8), 3=key_prefix (len32+utf8), 4=op (single op byte, 0..3), 5=keyspace_scope (len32+utf8). The layout is per-kind, not uniform TLV. This is a materially DIFFERENT vocabulary from the amulet's {exp,scope,audience,resource,tbl,kpfx}.

MACAROON-V2 expiry granularity is ONE SECOND (unix epoch seconds) and the comparison is STRICT: the README states 'strict now < expiry', and chain-refuse-expired.json pins now == expiry == 1752451200 as expect "refuse:CaveatFailed:time_before" (i.e. expiry is EXCLUSIVE - the opposite boundary convention from the amulet's inclusive 'now > exp'). A time-limited fallback in minutes IS expressible in macaroon-v2 and is NOT expressible in the amulet dialect.

MACAROON-V2 supplies 'now' as a VECTOR/VERIFIER-CONTEXT VALUE, not from a clock: every chain vector's input.context carries an explicit "now": 1752451200 alongside key/keyspace/op/resource. So in BOTH dialects the expiry clock is an injected caller-supplied value. OPEN QUESTION: the production call sites that populate this context are outside my slice (the named MacaroonV2Verifier is in Olamnit.Shared/Kv/, not Yngenios/Seal/) and I could not verify what clock they use.

MACAROON-V2 has a scope-like caveat already: keyspace_scope (tag 5), enforced by equality against the verifier-supplied context value "keyspace" (context {"keyspace": "ks-main"} vs caveat {kind: keyspace_scope, scope: "ks-main"} -> ok). Both sides move by V; the identity STILL HOLDS and audit.Holds stays true. I constructed this counterexample against the code rather than accepting 'by construction'.

What PoolAudit ACTUALLY catches is exactly two defect classes: (1) POOL OVERDRAW — sum of MintBody.FundingPoolUCoin exceeds sum of AgingBody.DecayedDeltaUCoin (returns Holds=false, 'pool overdrawn'); (2) an INTRA-DAG conservation break surfaced by VerifyAllConservation(). It catches NO defect in mint authorization, endorsement, provenance, identity, or rate policy.

The shipped forgery test confirms the boundary rather than closing it: PoolAuditTests's only forged-WAL case ('PoolOverdraw_FailsTheAudit_WhenForgedIntoTheWal') forges a mint funded 500 from POOL / 0 fresh. There is no test in my sources that forges a FRESH-funded mint into the WAL — the case that passes the audit. (Vocabulary searched in Olamnit.Coin.Tests/Ledger/: 'forge', 'forged', 'Mallory', 'bypass', 'Append(', 'Holds'.)

CoinDag.VerifyConservation is INTRA-DAG only: `live + decayed + spent == MintedValue`, where MintedValue is taken from the mint op that created the DAG (CoinDag ctor). A forged mint's DAG therefore satisfies it trivially at creation (root live == MintedValue). The DAG invariant is arithmetic self-consistency, not legitimacy of the root value.

SPLIT OF THE SMALLEST DENOMINATION IS REFUSED. ValidateSplit requires b.K >= 2 and b.Children.Count == b.K (else RejectedMalformed), then requires parentValue.TryFloorSplit(K) to succeed; TryFloorSplit returns false when `UCoin < k`. A 1-microcoin leaf therefore cannot split for any legal k>=2 — refused as RejectedConservation. The floor is structural, in MicroCoin, not a policy knob.

MERGE OF SMALLEST-DENOMINATION UNITS IS PERMITTED, under four conditions: >=2 parents; parents pairwise distinct; every parent a LIVE leaf; and Merged.ValueUCoin == the exact sum. Violations map to RejectedMalformed / RejectedUnknownRef / RejectedConservation respectively. Merging N 1-microcoin leaves of one mint is admissible.

MERGE ACROSS DISTINCT MINT DAGs IS REFUSED as RejectedMalformed ('v1: merge within one mint's DAG (per-coin lineage)'). Split cannot cross a DAG by construction (one ParentRef). Consequence for any batch/epoch minting design: reward units minted under DIFFERENT mint ids can never be consolidated into one leaf — holdings fragment permanently per mint.

The same one-mint-DAG restriction binds the SPEND leg twice: BalanceValidator refuses 'spend leg crosses mint DAGs - one mint per leg', and ValidateSpendProjection refuses RejectedMalformed. PaymentPlanner works around it by emitting one leg (and one commit id, and one E3PC witness round) PER MINT DAG. Per-mint fragmentation therefore scales the number of witnessed spend rounds.
Split and merge are BOTH additionally refused (RejectedReserved) when a parent leaf is reserved by an in-flight gated spend, via the reservation callback the SpendGate attaches at construction.
